items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Guy Kelly and Ray Allen come along together see. And Lee Collin. Them three come behind. Buddy 15 and me and Louie and Chris Kelly and Sam Morgan all of them in front of them. That's true. Just like Buddy Bowling was in front of me. I didn't know them both.

ctx.x: Sure. Sure, I know him. Where was he from? Do you remember anybody? Tell him he's from Milwaukee. I don't know. I don't know. Guys, that guy didn't tell you where the real home was. But we had a fella named Ed Ellis used to play trombone. Talked properly, you know. Every time somebody asked him, he was a little bit of a guitar.

I was wondering about somebody at that. Did you know Jimmy Blank, the piano player? Sure. I know him. But stuff says New York. So I asked him again, he says, tell him my home is in Philly. So he got sick, see. And he got really sick. Didn't nobody know what to do for everybody. So where was his people and everything. So he called his wife. His wife was named Stella. He said, what is it? He said, I told you all my home was in Philly and I told you all my home was in New York. He said, but I wish you'd call my…
I believe he left there in 22 didn't he? Joe, I think before then, 1918. Yeah, I didn't know him. He was in the Army when he left here again. Sure, I didn't know him.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: The guy played pretty stuff. He was the first one that made this. He played that in the blues.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. What about Guy Kelly? Did he finger fast or not?
Well, not too fair. The guy played pretty stuff. He was the first one that made this. He played that in the blues. I mean, in the blues now.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Well they played with Stone band in Chicago, all them guys

ctx.x: I can't place him, I'll play him.
Well they played with Stone band in Chicago, all them guys, he had a nice band there man. And then he left Chicago and went to New York see, and stood around they playing.
Who else did you play gigs with in New York?
